clue.text: Being a showman, this person's flaunting spare port

parts.note: 'this person is', said by the setter, is I'M

indicators.note: flaunting suggests the letters of 'spare' are tossed about and paraded in a new order

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a famous port

explanation.surface: Someone showing off a spare bottle of port, being something of a showman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flaunting' is an unusual anagram signal: the letters are paraded in a new order. 'Being a' simply links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical producer or promoter is a classic showman.

clue.text: Spice coats the carving knife

indicators.note: coats means the spice wraps around the other word, holding it inside

parts.note: mace is a spice made from nutmeg husks
the letters of the word 'the', which the parse needs in the order H, E, T

explanation.surface: A spice crust seasons the meat before the carving knife comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coats' signals containment, but the clue's 'the' must go in scrambled, a liberty the setter takes without any anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad heavy blade used for chopping and cutting, a large knife.

clue.text: Male's in difficulty with a dance

indicators.note: 's stands for 'is', and 'is in' places the male letter inside the next word

parts.note: rub means a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: A man struggles to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: RUB for 'difficulty' comes from Hamlet's 'there's the rub'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance, so an example of the broader category.

clue.text: Secrets escaped when ringing about ancient coin

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the enclosed letters are read from right to left
ringing means encircling, so the two words surround the answer's letters

explanation.surface: Secrets got out when a bell was rung over an old coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escaped' looks like an anagram signal, but the coin sits backwards inside 'Secrets escaped': 'when ringing' encloses it and 'about' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman coin worth a quarter of a denarius, an ancient piece of money.

clue.text: In children's story, strange pets still disturbed family

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of 'pets still' are stirred into a new order

parts.note: kin means one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: In a fairy tale, oddly calm pets unsettle the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' signals the anagram; 'strange' looks like a second one but gives RUM, British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grimm fairy tale about a little man who spins straw into gold bears this title.

clue.text: Fortune accompanies old church cat

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
one's lot is one's fortune or destiny

explanation.surface: Luck goes hand in hand with an ancient church moggy.
explanation.walkthrough: Though 'Fortune' comes first, it is placed last; 'accompanies' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotted wild feline of the Americas is one kind of cat.

clue.text: Time of day nobleman mainly collects son

indicators.note: collects means the shortened nobleman gathers the son letter inside
mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a duke is a high-ranking nobleman

explanation.surface: An aristocrat picks up his boy at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims DUKE to DUK, and 'collects' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The darkening part of evening just after sunset, a time of the day.

clue.text: Withdraw from office, committee being content to break up

indicators.note: being content means the committee abbreviation is the contents, sitting inside the other word

parts.note: to depose a ruler is to remove them from office

explanation.surface: A committee happy enough to dissolve itself after someone is ousted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' reads as 'satisfied' but here means 'contents', what is held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To rot is to disintegrate or fall apart, a sense of breaking up.

clue.text: Ale is repeatedly drunk in European region once

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling about into a new order
repeatedly means the little word 'is' is written out twice

explanation.surface: Beer is drunk again and again in some old corner of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles IS, and 'drunk' shuffles ALE ISIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical territory in central Europe, now mostly in Poland, the definition's former region.

clue.text: Scotsmen to do a turn, using fiddle

indicators.note: doing a turn means the word faces the other way, read from right to left

parts.note: Macs is an informal name for Scotsmen

explanation.surface: Scots perform a turn while playing the fiddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to do a turn' reverses MACS.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddle is a swindle or racket, a dishonest scheme.

clue.text: Inventive guy adapted meals to accommodate superior horse

indicators.note: to accommodate means the rearranged meals takes a letter inside it
adapted means the letters of 'meals' are altered into another order

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for upper-class, superior
a colt is a young male horse

explanation.surface: Someone reworks meals to fit in a fine horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' signals the anagram and 'to accommodate' the insertion; U for upper-class is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The American inventor of the revolver, so an inventive man.

clue.text: Type of seed mother's found back in York perhaps

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the bishop's seat

parts.note: York is an archbishop's see, a diocese

indicators.note: back means the mother's word is turned around

parts.note: ma is mother, so mother's is MA'S

explanation.surface: Mum's seeds turn up in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: York is the seat of an archbishop, so it is an example of a SEE; 'back' reverses MA'S to SAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A small oily seed used in baking and for oil, one kind of seed.

clue.text: European brought in manuscripts on college course latterly?

indicators.note: on means the manuscripts come after the college in an across answer

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school, founded as a college

indicators.note: brought in means the European letter is placed inside the manuscripts

explanation.surface: A European reads manuscripts on a college course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks academic but is a meal course; 'latterly' and the question mark point to dessert, a late course.
explanation.definitionFit: A dessert of strawberries, cream and meringue, served as a late course of a meal.

clue.text: Staff talk about trimming outside piece of cartilage

parts.note: staff means workers, men

indicators.note: trimming outside means the first and last letters are cut off

parts.note: to discuss something is to talk about it

explanation.surface: Workers discuss cutting cartilage away in surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimming outside' cuts DISCUSS to ISCUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescent-shaped pad of cartilage in the knee joint, a piece of cartilage.

clue.text: Fretful introduction by Irishman perhaps, one on hospital department

parts.note: an Irishman might introduce himself as 'I'm Pat', Pat being a typical Irish name
I is the Roman numeral for one
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: An Irishman introduces himself nervously on arriving at a hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restless and unable to wait calmly is fretful.

clue.text: Lady heading off somewhere in Middle East

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A lady sets off for the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the W from WOMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultanate on the Arabian peninsula, a country in the Middle East.

clue.text: Health resort rouses retired type

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a health resort

indicators.note: retired means going back, so the word is read in reverse in this down clue

parts.note: fires means rouses or stirs up

explanation.surface: A spa wakes up a type who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reverses FIRES to SERIF.
explanation.definitionFit: A typeface without the small strokes at the ends of letters is a kind of type.

clue.text: Mark goes inside to drink punch

indicators.note: goes inside means the mark letter is placed within the drinking word

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does
M is the abbreviation for mark, as in the old German currency

explanation.surface: Mark goes indoors for a drink of punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punch' looks like a drink but is the verb meaning to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for striking someone with the fist.

clue.text: A married woman, followed by Oscar at separate intervals — that's sweet

parts.words: married woman, followed by Oscar at separate intervals
parts.note: Mrs is a married woman's title, and an O (Oscar in the radio alphabet) follows each of its three letters in turn

explanation.surface: A wife followed every so often by Oscar is a sweet thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'followed by Oscar at separate intervals' puts O after each letter of MRS: MO, RO, SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetened dark sherry; the word describes a sweet style of wine.

clue.text: Sort of naiveté, some might say

indicators.note: some might say signals that the word for naivety is spoken, giving the answer's sound

parts.note: innocence is naive lack of worldliness

explanation.surface: Some regard a kind of naivety as such.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning in some way, to a degree, much like 'sort of'.

clue.text: Italian city market — northwards near roundabout?

parts.note: a sale is a market where goods are sold

indicators.note: northwards means read upwards in this down clue, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a roundabout is circular, so the round letter O

explanation.surface: An Italian city's market lies north, close to a traffic roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northwards' reverses O and NR to give RNO; the question mark flags O for 'roundabout' as a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A port city on the south-west coast of Italy.

clue.text: Pop artist fights against everything, audibly

indicators.note: audibly signals that the two words are spoken and give the answer's sound

parts.note: to war is to fight against, and the whole is everything

explanation.surface: A pop star rails against the world, loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop artist' suggests a singer, but it is the painter of soup cans.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy, the American figure of the Pop Art movement, a pop artist.

clue.text: Left one to lie in grass, painting?

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: to lie in means the one letter rests inside the informer word

parts.note: grass and rat are both slang for an informer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone left behind to lie in the grass, as if in a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like a lawn but is slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted likeness of a person is one kind of painting, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Hamper, comprising small spongy dessert, Roger removed

indicators.note: removed means the Roger letter is taken out of the dessert

parts.note: a trifle is a layered dessert with sponge cake
Roger is R in the old radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A picnic basket containing a little sponge pudding, Roger having taken his away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a picnic basket but is the verb meaning restrict.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict or suppress is to hold back, as a verb meaning impede.

clue.text: Drive Sprite, bearing left

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous sprite
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A sprite drives, bearing left.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge or force forward is to drive.

clue.text: Maybe rib bartender's bike

parts.note: a rib is an example of a bone
a cocktail shaker is the bartender's tool

explanation.surface: A spare rib belonging to a barman, perhaps, and his bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: An old bicycle with solid tyres and a rough ride, a kind of bike.

clue.text: Particular hairstyle wanted each month

parts.note: per means for each, as in per day

explanation.surface: A certain hairdo is booked monthly.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemically set wave is a specific style of hair.

clue.text: Linesman possibly starts to puff over extra time

indicators.note: starts to means taking the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A football linesman puffs as the match goes to extra time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linesman' looks like a football official, but a writer of lines of verse is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of verse lines, hence 'possibly', is a linesman in a punning sense.

clue.text: Tall chap, 27

definitions.note: 27 refers to the answer at 27 across, a verse writer

parts.note: long means tall
a fellow is a chap

explanation.surface: A tall man is referred to by a cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Wadsworth, the American verse writer of Hiawatha, an example of the 27 across.
